    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
    • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.
    • The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

    The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

    The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

    However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

    The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

    ‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

    Industry observers note that the incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

    Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

    It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

    Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

    Welcome to our Live Comments section, where upcoming comments will appear automatically.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Sources indicate that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Sources indicate that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout rapidly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    In a recent development, zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    Industry observers note that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Sources indicate that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    It has been revealed that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see newly introduced highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    • Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

    Published: 03:53 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 04:20 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

    England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

    Although Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams managed to claw two back for this year's World Cup winners, England held on with a backs-to-the-wall effort in the closing stages, courtesy of a few fine saves from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

    After England's victory, which called an end to Spain's historic 43-game unbeaten run, Bellingham was spotted celebrating with his model girlfriend Ashlyn inside the stadium.

    Wearing a beaming smile, he went over to embrace both the 28-year-old American and his father Mark as the family soaked up the celebrations in the stands.

    The Real Madrid superstar has largely kept his relationship with Ashlyn private since the pair were first linked in early 2025.

    Jude Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashlyn Castro celebrate England's superb win over Spain.

    The Real Madrid star then caught up with his dad Mark on a special night for the Bellinghams.

    Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California (@instagram/ashlyncastro).

    Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California who boasts over one million followers on Instagram, sharing fashion and beauty content online.

    Spanish media waxed lyrical about Bellingham's display on the night, claiming he was 'determined to make a statement' at the stadium of Real Madrid's rivals Atletico.

    Newspaper AS wrote: 'If anyone felt the match was crucial, it was Jude Bellingham. He stepped onto the Metropolitano pitch determined to make a statement, to impose his usual footballing and physical prowess.

    'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'.

    It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

    Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

    England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

    The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.

    #73817. Data center construction costs soar 13% in 2026

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (505 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Data center construction costs soar 13% in 2026

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S.
    • All that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a upcoming report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management company.
    • The report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S. this year, driven by the need for computing power for artificial intelligence, grew well beyond the supply of powered land and the labor to build these structures. It also pushed timelines and risk for contractors.

    All that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a upcoming report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management company. The gain this year was about three times the last ten-year average.

    The report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets. It also included a survey of 400 experts in the global data center industry.

    While there was some stabilization in cost inflation this year, it was not enough to offset the huge growth in not just demand but speed of construction and delivery.

    "More aggressive schedules tie to contractors in particular and subcontractors baking in more risk allowances in their pricing," noted Paul Barry, North America data center lead for Turner & Townsend. "So whether that's acceleration allowances, whether that's more overtime and labor attraction allowances, even just higher fees for taking on the risk of delivering at a faster pace than what they would traditionally take on.".

    All of those things, combined with the spike in demand and the strain on the supply chain, translate into higher costs, he added.

    Capital expenditure on global data centers is projected to rise from about $800 billion this year to $1.8 trillion per year in 2050, according to a recent report from PwC. The U.S. is expected to capture almost half of all global investment in AI infrastructure, which includes both data centers and chips.

    Power is, of course, key to all data centers, and 56% of those surveyed by Turner & Townsend globally said it was a major obstacle to delivery. Just over half said utility connections typically take between one and two years, and almost a third reported timeframes of over two years. Costs for power vary regionally — from $15.01 per watt in Silicon Valley to $10.51 per watt in Dallas, based on a typical 60-megawatt design.As with every type of construction in the U.S., labor continues to be a significant headwind. Just over one quarter of respondents said their contractor capacity, that is, the ability to manage construction backlogs, was sufficient.

    Sources indicate that going forward, Barry noted he expects costs to moderate somewhat, with cost increases in the 6% to 10% range in the next year. A lot of the major projects have already started or are starting now, so cost risk has been baked into those contracts.

    "If this demand continues, then there'll be more continued flow of project starts and so on, but I think we've hit a major surge in 2026, especially of upcoming big major projects that have been procured," noted Barry.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (379 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens 'tremendous tax'

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (379 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday said U.S.
    • "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump mentioned at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.
    • "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump remarked.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday said U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so.

    "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump mentioned at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.

    "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump remarked. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here.".

    Industry observers note that trump's latest push for more data-center construction in the U.S. came despite Americans repeatedly stating — and showing with their votes — that they dislike the structures.

    CNBC's All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% of respondents said they would support one.

    In a recent development, if Trump follows through on his threat to clamp down on overseas data center construction, he will have to contend with the fact that numerous U.S. tech giants — including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — have already built them in other countries.

    International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements.

    Trump stated Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them.".

    "We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They're tremendous assets," Trump mentioned.

    Representatives at cloud providers Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

    Trump's remarks came a day after Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for a trilateral summit that appeared to produce few concrete deliverables on an array of pressing global complications.

    Xi "congratulated me on how well we're doing" in artificial intelligence, Trump said, using his preferred term "super intelligence," which he said the Chinese president also likes better.

    — CNBC's Jordan Novet and Annie Palmer contributed reporting.

    #73800. AI is changing software engineering — and some developers miss the struggle

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (963 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    AI is changing software engineering — and some developers miss the struggle

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that when Gemma Rodgers began her computer science degree in 2002, software engineering was seen as a future-proof and lucrative career.
    • It's an industry that has always moved fast, Rodgers, a software developer based in the U.K., told CNBC.
    • As AI coding tools help engineers write, debug and test code faster than ever, some are mourning the job they used to have.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that when Gemma Rodgers began her computer science degree in 2002, software engineering was seen as a future-proof and lucrative career. It appealed to people who enjoyed getting into the weeds of code, tracking down bugs and building programs from scratch.

    It's an industry that has always moved fast, Rodgers, a software developer based in the U.K., told CNBC. But the arrival of artificial intelligence has accelerated the pace, with AI tools now part of the daily work of every software engineer she knows. In a 2026 Stack Overflow survey, 83% of software developer respondents said they use at least one AI tool.

    As AI coding tools help engineers write, debug and test code faster than ever, some are mourning the job they used to have. Rodgers has always loved the sense of accomplishment that comes from piecing together different parts of code to find a solution, particularly when she's spent days, or even weeks, trying to fix a stubborn bug.

    "The sense of joy and fun that I used to experience by having a challenge and then having to work that out, it's been removed somewhat," she said. "Now you can sometimes do it in a few prompts, and it's great — but it's a breadcrumb of joy, not a full meal of joy.".

    Rodgers is not alone in feeling nostalgic about the not-so-old days. Software engineers have taken to social media to describe missing their old way of working, when they could get into a flow state with code for hours at a time.

    It has been revealed that still, AI tools can be useful and have lowered the barrier to entry significantly. "It's becoming an industry where a lot of people have been able to thrive who wouldn't necessarily have been able to thrive 10 years ago, five years ago, even three years ago," Rodgers stated.

    It's also notable that the core skills engineers have traditionally learned on the job are not lost, she noted. AI tools and internet services can go down unexpectedly, and engineers still need to know how to investigate problems and work through solutions themselves.

    "The sorts of skills that we were taught years ago are kind of being lost because [engineers are] having to just churn work out," Rodgers added.

    The job itself is changing, too. James Broadhead, chief technology officer of AI decision-making company Taktile, told CNBC that engineers who might previously have spent three weeks building a prototype can now generate 10 in an afternoon. The hardest part of that, he remarked, is "having the judgment to decide which of those are any good.".

    "The [AI] agents are spitting out so much code that [engineers] haven't read it all anymore," Broadhead remarked. "It used to be you'd build up a sense of comfort and awareness of how the whole code base was structured, but now the whole thing changes all the time.".

    Joshua Wöhle, CEO of London-based AI training tech giant Mindstone, told CNBC he sees a growing divide between workers who know how to use AI effectively and those who don't.

    Industry observers note that the industry used to talk about "10X engineers," he noted, who were dramatically more productive than their peers. Now, AI is widening that gap even further to produce "100X engineers.".

    It has been revealed that wöhle believes companies will increasingly have to decide whether to help employees catch up with AI or prioritize those who can get the most out of it. But he also understands why some engineers might struggle to adapt.

    The people who once excelled at the job were often those who loved writing and working through code, he said, and those are not necessarily the current top performers.

    Industry observers note that "That's the grief that is very, very real," Wöhle said. "The thing you love doing is no longer the thing the firm should be paying for, to a degree, because it's no longer adding the value to the company that it used to.".

    In a recent development, but not every engineer sees the move away from hands-on coding as a bad thing. Chris Sees, a software engineer of more than 20 years and CEO of London-based virtual office company Hoxton Mix, told CNBC that AI gives developers more time to tackle interesting problems. He views AI as a capable junior engineer that still needs supervision.

    According to recent reports, "The important thing is knowing what to delegate and when human judgement is needed," Sees mentioned. "We'd be silly to think AI gets everything right, and I know I get a lot of satisfaction out of proving and spotting where it has gone wrong.".

    Even so, Sees worries about what happens to the next generation of engineers if AI takes over the routine coding and debugging through which they traditionally learned. Those tasks are "where you learn lessons and build scar tissue," he noted, and companies need to make sure AI becomes part of the learning process, rather than a shortcut.

    For Rodgers, what matters is having control over how she uses the technology. As a self-employed developer, she can use AI to automate the parts of a project she finds tedious, while keeping the more interesting problem-solving for herself.

    According to recent reports, she believes there's something vital about working through a difficult problem rather than immediately outsourcing it to technology. Friction and discomfort, she noted, are vital parts of the human experience.

    According to recent reports, "As humans, we need to feel accomplished in something and part of accomplishment requires challenge," she stated. "Unless we are able to work that through in so many different aspects of life, then you never get the full force of the good feeling on the other side.".

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • Industry observers note that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Industry observers note that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession proposal, makes it worse.

    Industry observers note that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a major haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the manufacturer's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Industry observers note that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    #73784. Tech Report: Europe's cyber weak spot is the everyday businesses nobody thought to protect

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1017 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Europe's cyber weak spot is the everyday businesses nobody thought to protect

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act.
    • Industry observers note that attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November.
    • Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act. But it wasn't fast enough.

    Industry observers note that attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November. The affected stores had been scheduled for security upgrades just two days later, a organization spokesperson told CNBC.

    Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.

    Experts are warning that a combination of known vulnerabilities, basic security failures and ambiguity over whether suppliers or their clients are responsible are making things worse, as AI makes cyber threats faster and more sophisticated.

    Guy Segal, CEO of cybersecurity firm Sygnia, told CNBC that his firm handled 285% more incidents in October than a year earlier, with demand forcing it to turn away some businesses seeking emergency assistance.

    "It's going to get worse before it's going to get better," Segal said.

    The recent cyberattacks targeted refrigeration systems across hundreds of European supermarkets, remotely altering temperature settings and forcing retailers to discard spoiled food.

    France has since accused a cyber unit with links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps of the attacks, an allegation Tehran denies.

    Fredrik Blix, a cybersecurity researcher at Stockholm University, told CNBC that thousands of industrial control systems remain accessible over the public internet, sometimes despite manufacturers' warnings.

    Segal said that basic cyber protection measures such as multi-factor authentication and basic network segmentation are more important than ever.

    He said risks to major civic infrastructure like the electrical grid were front of mind and so "usually pretty well protected.".

    In a recent development, "There are always those civil supply chain components that are way, way less protected. Could be supermarkets, could be gas stations, could be… the screens on the Tube," Segal noted, referring to London's underground rail system.

    The supermarket attacks highlighted "this is the new normal, and definitely it's a wake-up call for every tech giant out there," Segal added.

    It has been revealed that segal said that inexpensive AI tools mean technical expertise and resources are no longer needed to launch attacks. He described one recent incident in which clients suffered breaches within six hours of a vulnerability becoming known, as perpetrators used AI to act faster — a process that might have taken weeks a year earlier.

    Segal, whose firm helps companies respond to breaches and strengthen their defenses, warned that businesses without prearranged incident-response support could struggle to secure emergency assistance, as overwhelmed cybersecurity firms prioritize existing clients.

    In one case, he stated, Sygnia had to turn down a firm because no response teams were available. Segal added that the company in question had already been turned down by ten other providers.

    Jacob Silverman, CEO of risk advisory firm Kroll, told CNBC earlier this month that the manufacturer was operating at full capacity in its incident-response business amid what he described as "the most rapid uptick in threat activity that we've ever seen.".

    Segal argued that retailers should treat cybersecurity risks with the same seriousness as fire safety and food hygiene, including when outsourcing maintenance.

    Industry observers note that when Ahold Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were attacked on Nov. 2, it exposed how different independent store operators had responded to the warnings following the earlier attacks in France.

    Retailers had been warned about the vulnerabilities following earlier attacks in France, and those that implemented the recommended protections were spared, CEO Frans Muller told investors in an earnings call earlier this month, but smaller operators with fewer technical resources had struggled to make the necessary changes.

    Coop, whose stores are owned by regional consumer cooperatives or operated by franchises, told CNBC that public attention on the recent attacks was the main driver of security improvements. It said the vulnerability at the affected stores had since been addressed.

    Industry observers note that the financial consequences of cyberattacks can be substantial. Ahold Delhaize told investors in November that a separate October cyberattack on its online operations and supply chain would reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million euros ($219 million).

    Danish shipping giant Maersk, which suffered an estimated $250 million to $300 million in losses from the 2017 NotPetya cyberattack, has spent nearly a decade strengthening its defenses.

    CEO Vincent Clerc told CNBC earlier this month that the experience had prompted significant investment in security capabilities, but warned that AI was enabling attackers to become more effective.

    "Everybody is in a race" to boost defenses, he said.

    Research by cybersecurity firm Censys found that the number of internet-exposed refrigeration controllers made by Danfoss and Copeland exposed to cyber hacking fell 53% globally between Oct. 9 and Nov. 5.

    However, more than 3,100 remained exposed, and Censys noted it could not determine whether the decline reflected permanent security improvements or equipment simply being taken offline.

    A Copeland spokesperson confirmed that some of its refrigeration systems were affected by the vulnerability and remarked it had contacted customers to reinforce cybersecurity guidance, including keeping devices off the public internet and updating software.

    Danfoss didn't respond to CNBC requests for comment.

    In the U.K., a covert cybersecurity operation has been underway to protect tens of thousands of refrigeration systems at supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants and other businesses, the BBC reported on Friday. After researchers discovered a major vulnerability in late October, cybersecurity specialists, IT teams and the U.K.'s National Cyber Security Centre worked to alert dozens of companies and secure their systems before hackers could exploit the flaw.

    The EU's Cyber Resilience Act will also impose stricter security requirements on manufacturers of connected products from December 2027.

    But the legislation does not require all existing equipment to be made compliant with the newly introduced standards.

    Blix told CNBC on Nov. 6 that European authorities should take a more proactive approach to reducing vulnerabilities by identifying exposed industrial control systems and contacting their operators before attacks occur.

    "What worries me is that we don't really do anything," he remarked, adding that "we are shuffling a lot of papers" and "doing a lot of risk assessments" but failing to take meaningful action.

    So much for buying the dip.As the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq-100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 19% from highs as of midday Friday, the single biggest options trade of the day was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has a long way more to fall.Around 12:30 E.T., someone spent $93 million buying 20,000 380-strike puts expiring Sep. 17, 2027, according to trading data reviewed by SpotGamma and Volland, options-analytics platforms that both show the trade as a likely opening position, with volume exceeding existing open interest in the contract. The trade bets that the index will fall below $380, a nearly 8% decline from its current level. The SMH is off 40% from its recent all-time highs.

    "That trade stands out big-time," wrote Jason DeLorenzo, founder and owner of Volland. "It is either a hedge or speculative, but either way it isn't a vote of confidence."The puts were bought for $46.50 a piece, an arguably expensive choice for a downside bet with volatility in the ETF trading at 70.

    Recent findings suggest that "You're paying a metric ton of Vega for that thing," added SpotGamma's Brent Kochuba, referring to the contract's sensitivity to changes in volatility of the underlying chip ETF. "Maybe they were a forced buyer, or maybe they're actually selling this, which can still be the case even though the price shows it happening closer to the ask.".

    The semiconductor index headed for a 9% drop this week alone.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
    • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
    • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

    AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

    Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

    That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand remarked everything you need to know about this moment...

    Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

    Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

    Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

    Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

    Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

    According to recent reports, united’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

    Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

    Four minutes of added time to be played...

    United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

    For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

    In a recent development, martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

    Industry observers note that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

    Sources indicate that big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

    Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

    Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

    Sources indicate that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

    Industry observers note that manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by upcoming signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

    Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

    Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

    Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

    For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

    In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

    According to recent reports, milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

    United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

    Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

    Sources indicate that all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

    Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

    Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

    De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

    The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

    Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

    Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

    United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

    Recent findings suggest that shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

    Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

    United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

    A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

    Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

    In a recent development, A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

    According to recent reports, estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

    Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

    Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

    Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

    It has been revealed that united make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

    Recent findings suggest that szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

    In a recent development, the players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely upcoming cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

    According to recent reports, we are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

    In a recent development, manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

    Sources indicate that marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

    Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

    The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the newly introduced campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

    Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

    So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

    Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

    Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

    At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    In a recent development, “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

    Recent findings suggest that at the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri remarked Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

    Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

    Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, newly introduced signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

    #73777. Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO couldn't escape the stock market correction

    Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO couldn't escape the stock market correction

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that no one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the organization.
    • The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, notes Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).
    • "The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez remarked on "ETF Edge" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that no one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the organization. Deal size and pricing were signs of what IPO experts say was insatiable demand for "ANT" shares. But what came within a day is something that investors better get used to: anxiety in the stock market about valuations being assigned to artificial intelligence revenue and business models that should keep Anthropic shares volatile in the period ahead.

    The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, notes Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).

    "The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez remarked on "ETF Edge" on Friday.

    And in the case of Anthropic, which finished trading Friday down 9%, the valuation anxiety becomes "so much more prevalent," she added, because it is a fresh stock.

    Industry observers note that it is not just any fresh stock, but one that has Wall Street noting downside risks in research notes likely never seen before, and which may be the greatest understatements in the history of earnings analysis. "Anthropic could develop AI systems which become fully autonomous and wipe out humanity which may lead to a serious decline in earnings," Seaport Research Partners analyst wrote Jay Goldberg wrote on Nov. 18.

    "It was challenging firm to value ... and it's very richly valued," Marquez remarked. "We're seeing something more reasonable and investors grappling now with where should this company actually be valued," she added.

    Industry observers note that the fact that Anthropic pulled off the deal in this market and was able to command the price it did was an achievement, according to Yuri Khodjamirian, chief investment officer at Tema ETFs, which offers multiple funds that invest in pre-IPO shares of companies and held Anthropic in its Tema Photonics & Optical ETF (LAZR) well before IPO day. "We have to remember they pulled off a very large IPO in the middle of a very severe market with the volatility in the tech sector specifically," Khodjamirian remarked on "ETF Edge.".

    Industry observers note that khodjamirian says the investor demand for AI remains, but amid a reassessment of returns. And he says an equally hard task has now begun for Anthropic. Investors are unwinding positions in everything from tech stocks to gold and bitcoin, and repositioning for 2027 based on their new outlooks. "We are in a bit of vacuum," he remarked.

    "From here on the market is trying trying to figure out what direction to go in," Khodjamirian mentioned, whether that is based on Fed policy, geopolitics, the midterm elections results, or the AI trade. "In many cases, the chief investment officers I speak to, and the clients, say 'I'm just gonna take some risk off and wait and see until I get more info.' And with the Anthropic, the revenue picture and how the AI adoption curve progresses will be a vital stat to watch," he added.

    Plenty of value has already been wiped out in tech, according to Khodjamirian, but investors need newly introduced signals to buy. That doesn't just go for Anthropic but for much of the market's tech leadership. "One of the things most difficult for investors to understand right now is some of the leadership in the market that has been taken by semiconductor companies," he remarked, adding that the peak was 22% of S&P 500 earnings. But these companies, like Nvidia and Micron, have a very different earnings profile from the rest of the market.

    The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which was down over 10% on Friday and around 15% for the week, was on pace for its worst week since September 2001, according to CNBC data on Friday afternoon. It also lost 15% in one week of March 2020. The tech sector of the S&P 500, tracked by the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK), turned in its worst weekly performance since the Covid crash.

    Khodjamirian stated while these stocks may look cheap on a P/E basis right now after the heavy selling, that requires faith in the earnings estimates, which he indicates will be more notable as results are released for the next few years. "Right now it looks cheap, but will companies like Micron and Nvidia actually deliver?".

    Sources indicate that nvidia shares fell 14% on Friday, adding to its worst stretch of weekly performance since 2008. What's more, the single biggest trade in the options market on Friday was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF has a long way more to fall.

    In a recent development, and the same caution about the outlook goes for Anthropic, he remarked. "That's why we need to watch Anthropic's annual recurring revenue number, because it is a key part of puzzle," he said.

    Industry observers note that marquez said there is always hype in names like SpaceX and Anthropic when they go public, and it is hard to know whether the pricing of the deal is based on fundamentals, "but we just need more time and lots price discovery," she said. "It is not going to happen overnight," she added.

    Recent findings suggest that as an IPO researcher, she claims this "discernment" is a healthy thing for the markets. There are few cases to look to as comps for Anthropic, other than SpaceX, and before that, way back to Facebook's IPO in 2012. And neither example is one of quick recovery. SpaceX shares remain well below their first-day closing price more than five months after its IPO. Facebook (now Meta), meanwhile, "did not do well for the first year after going public and we see where it is now. It's just the nature of these disruptive tech companies that come to market," Marquez mentioned. "They lend themselves to more volatility and a longer period of price discovery for investors.".

    It has been revealed that all eyes will next be on Anthropic's rival OpenAI, which has suggested it will be ready to go public in 2027. Marquez remarked the reaction to the Anthropic deal may be a signal that it was "a good idea to wait, allowing themselves to build more quarters of better financials and improve fundamentals a bit before taking on a market that is really quite discerning.".

    According to recent reports, tema does not own shares of OpenAI in any of its ETFs. But, "I can't say it wont be," Khodjamirian noted. "They exist out there in the secondary market, and we will look at it, but we haven't made any decision. It depends on the ETF fit and if the portfolio manager wants to invest. We are always looking out for these interesting businesses but never just for the sake of private exposure," he added.

    Sources indicate that tema does own Databricks, Stripe, Kalshi and Polymarket across its funds. It also was an investor in SpaceX pre-IPO through its Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA).

    Recent findings suggest that khodjamirian said demand from public market investors to access these "generational businesses" will continue to be the case, despite the market volatility, and will more often come before IPO day. In fact, he pointed to the filing from the world's largest asset manager and one of the biggest ETF companies in the world, BlackRock, earlier this week. It wants to bring out a latest kind of exchange-traded product that would bring the ETF and interval fund structures together as a way to increase exposure to private companies, with shares trading on an exchange while the fund makes monthly repurchase offers.

    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the manufacturer's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks upcoming CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to rapidly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    It has been revealed that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the firm's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most vital ideas.

    WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Two of the — well, all of the crucial ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    Recent findings suggest that and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    An early breakdown in the polar vortex is threatening already depleted gas stocks

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex and a record-breaking El Niño event has put energy traders on alert this winter, with analysts warning the weather and climate phenomena could have an outsized impact on Europe.
    • Meteorologists are currently observing a record early breakdown of the polar vortex, a large-scale circulation of strong winds that typically keeps extremely cold air over the North Pole.
    • Changes in the strength and shape of the polar vortex can influence weather patterns much lower down in the atmosphere, potentially bringing in colder weather to parts of Europe and North America.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex and a record-breaking El Niño event has put energy traders on alert this winter, with analysts warning the weather and climate phenomena could have an outsized impact on Europe.

    Meteorologists are currently observing a record early breakdown of the polar vortex, a large-scale circulation of strong winds that typically keeps extremely cold air over the North Pole.

    Changes in the strength and shape of the polar vortex can influence weather patterns much lower down in the atmosphere, potentially bringing in colder weather to parts of Europe and North America.

    This year, however, the collapse of the stratospheric polar vortex, or SPV, is taking place at the same time as an unusually powerful El Niño, a climate event that can boost global temperatures and disrupt rainfall.

    According to recent reports, the collision of these two events raises the risk of a prolonged cold spell that could lift heating demand and force European countries to draw down already-low reserves faster. That would leave the continent more reliant on imported liquefied natural gas (LNG) at a time when supplies from the Middle East are disrupted.

    To be sure, Europe's natural gas storage levels started the winter at their lowest level in more than a decade.

    The International Energy Agency warned earlier this month that low European storage levels and limited storage options in several LNG-importing countries in Asia and South America could intensify the competition for cargoes and put upward pressure on prices during periods of high demand.

    Simon Lee, a lecturer in atmospheric science at the U.K.'s University of St Andrews, noted the combination of a sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) with an El Niño event is not necessarily unusual, but meteorologists had been expecting a polar vortex breakdown in February — not as early as November.

    The early SPV disruption is an "extremely rare" event that could influence winter weather in northwest Europe and the eastern U.S., Lee said, increasing the chance of colder conditions although likely not to the extent that a polar vortex event caused parts of Niagara Falls to partially freeze in January 2014.

    "Geopolitics and weather are the two key volatility drives for energy and now they seem to be happening at the same time — and that's always the biggest risk for markets," Florence Schmit, senior energy strategist at Rabobank, told CNBC.

    For months, meteorologists expected an El Niño event would result in a milder winter in Europe and relatively muted heating demand, Schmit stated, which was broadly seen as welcome news given ongoing concerns over the continent's tight regional supplies for gas and crude oil.

    In a recent development, the prospect of a colder-than-expected winter due to an early breakdown of the polar vortex could be "incredibly difficult" for Europe to navigate, Schmit warned. She noted that the region's gas storages have seen "very, very strong withdrawals" over the last two weeks, "which is quite unusual for this time of year.".

    "If you continue to see the same storage withdrawals over the next couple of months, that means energy prices will spike again — and they won't spike because of geopolitics. This time it will be the weather driving that spike and that volatility," Schmit noted.

    Sources indicate that european gas prices have soared to levels not seen since the 2022 energy crisis in recent weeks, notching 103.9 euros ($113.99) per megawatt hour in late October. European benchmark Dutch TTF futures for December delivery stood at around 87.28 euros on Friday afternoon.

    "We have never seen an early breakdown of the polar vortex and a super el Nino in the same winter so we have no historical precedent on how this will impact global gas demand," David Lewis, principal research analyst of gas and liquified natural gas at Wood Mackenzie, told CNBC by email.

    El Niño is commonly associated with milder winters, while a SSW event typically leads to colder temperatures and higher snowfall, Lewis stated, noting this could materialize in December and January within Europe.

    "So far, the start of the European winter heating season has been quite cold but more importantly has seen low wind speeds across Northern Europe," Lewis said.

    "The drawdown in stocks in the first half of November has been amongst the highest on record. With inventories starting the winter at their lowest level on record, any further deterioration in temperatures or wind speeds will have an outsized impact on European balances and lead to higher prices across Europe," he added.
