    James Harden played by far his best game in a Cleveland Cavaliers uniform on Friday night during NBA Cup group play.

    The 37-year-old guard erupted for 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers, a season high and his most since joining the Cavaliers amid the 2025-26 campaign.

    Recent findings suggest that cleveland (9-8) improved to 2-1 in Cup competition, knocking on the Miami Heat's door atop East Group B. Indiana (5-11), which trailed the Cavaliers by as many as 24 points, dropped to 1-2 in this year's NBA Cup.

    According to recent reports, harden shot 15 of 26 from the floor, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also finished 14 of 14 from the charity stripe and with six rebounds and six assists. The one-time NBA MVP and 11-time All-Star now has the third-most 50-plus-point games in NBA history. With 26 such performances, he passed the late Kobe Bryant (25) on Friday and now trails Michael Jordan (31) and Wilt Chamberlain (118) in that category.

    It has been revealed that while collecting his first 50-piece with the Cavaliers, Harden moved into ninth all-time for most combined NBA regular and postseason points. His handles were on full display. He rained down 3s, and he made an impact at the rim.

    Toronto came into Friday missing a trio of starters and on a six-game losing streak. Darko Rajaković's team was playing without RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles and, of course, Kawhi Leonard, who's still working his way back from a knee injury.

    And yet, the shorthanded Raptors (6-10) found a way on the road versus the Detroit Pistons (10-5) in NBA Cup action, ending their skid with a riveting 105-102 win.

    It's key to note that Detroit isn't at full strength, either. Jalen Duren remains sidelined with a hamstring issue. Plus, Duncan Robinson is out with a quad strain.

    According to recent reports, the absence of some star power didn't diminish what turned out to be an incredible matchup between two squads in East Group A and between a pair of former Montverde Academy teammates. Toronto's Scottie Barnes and Detroit's Cade Cunningham went toe-to-toe, particularly down the stretch.

    Recent findings suggest that cunningham, who clocked out with 23 points and nine assists, hit a go-ahead 3-pointer over Barnes with less than 20 seconds remaining. Then, with the Raptors down one point, Barnes drove on Cunningham and reclaimed the lead.

    Cunningham tried to answer back but ended up with nowhere to go with the ball after picking up his dribble en route to the basket. He passed it, and Toronto rookie Allen Graves nabbed a steal that helped wrap up the victory.

    Recent findings suggest that barnes had 29 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists. Graves, a first-round pick from Santa Clara making his first career start, piled up 20 points, 10 rebounds and 3 steals.

    It has been revealed that after that nail-biter, Toronto is 2-1 in East Group A, whereas Detroit is 1-1. The bottom dweller of the group, the Milwaukee Bucks (0-2 in NBA Cup play), was eliminated from knockout-round contention because the Raptors and Orlando Magic both won on Friday.

    The Magic left Brooklyn victorious 113-111, thanks to Franz Wagner, who scored 35 points on 13-of-25 shooting and knocked down a game-winning jumper with 2.4 ticks left against the Nets.

    Orlando is 3-0 in NBA Cup games this year.

    Tech outages are fueling a upcoming doomsday economy

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S.
    • Industry observers note that government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions.
    • It has been revealed that in recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Americans are shopping like there's no tomorrow.

    Recent findings suggest that A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S. energy grid.

    Industry observers note that government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions. Despite those assurances, consumers like Sabrina Cepeda are readying for a larger-scale technology blackout or other emergency event.

    It has been revealed that in recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity. The mother of three also replenished her backup stockpiles of non-perishable foods, hygiene products and allergy medicine in the event that her family is homebound for several days.

    In a recent development, "I have a way to keep my family fed, clean, hydrated, warm and safe," said Cepeda, 39. "You want to have these things and not need them, rather than need them and not have them.".

    The doomsday economy is catching a bid. Wall Street and retailers are taking note.

    Industry observers note that at least half a dozen major technology outages took place in the U.S. between Nov. 12 and Nov. 17. In that time frame, spending at brands specializing in emergency products spiked about 400% compared with the same period a year prior, according to card data analyzed exclusively for CNBC by Consumer Edge.

    At Ready America, which sells products like emergency survival kits, prepackaged water and high-calorie food bars, sales through e-commerce platforms have seen a roughly five-fold increase in recent days. In addition, corporate customers who keep the Vista, California-based firm's supplies in their offices in case of emergency have called in to order more.

    The manufacturer has rarely seen this much demand since the Covid pandemic sent Americans into lockdown more than six years ago, said Ready America President Trevyn Reese. As a result, Ready America asked its suppliers to scale up production. The family-owned business has faced a shortage of water purification tablets, and redirected shoppers to alternative offerings like prepackaged water pouches.

    "With everything going on in the news right now, we've seen a large spike of people wanting to get prepared," mentioned Reese.

    While the string of outages brought power-related concerns to a boiling point, data shows that worries had been bubbling under the surface for weeks.

    Shoppers began significantly ramping up buying from emergency preparedness brands late last month, according to Consumer Edge. Around that time, Fox News reported that the Pentagon was preparing U.S. military bases to operate for at least 90 days without external support. Exacerbating those fears was the ongoing war with Iran that President Donald Trump signaled could ramp back up.

    In a recent development, firearm trade group NSSF stated that gun sales rose about 8% in October from the same month a year prior. Retailers and gun manufacturers have anecdotally reported that demand has remained elevated into November, which NSSF said can be attributed to a combination of uncertainty tied to the midterm election and the recent outages.

    Sources indicate that "If people are investing in firearms and ammunition, they're telling you very directly, with their wallet, what their priority is," remarked Mark Oliva, NSSF's managing director of public affairs. "You're literally investing in a product that's going to be able to protect your life and protect the lives of your family.".

    Now, the doomsday talk has begun making its way to Wall Street.

    Mizuho told clients on Monday that consumer worries about the outages — coupled with what the bank called "apocalyptic concerns" swirling on social media — drove shoppers to stock up on emergency supplies at Costco. As a result, Mizuho said it expects a key measure of non-fuel sales growth for Costco in November to rise above 10% for the first time since 2022.

    In a recent development, and RBC noted so-called doomsday prepping has had a "real impact" on buying behavior around the globe over recent weeks. Still, the Canadian bank reported that the trend has so far boosted sales for only a small basket of items, such as shelf-stable proteins, water purification products and dry-pantry foods.

    Industry observers note that clients of Richard McWhorter, a private wealth advisor at SRM, have been rushing to Costco to buy goods in bulk and splurging for power generators. McWhorter said he's also fielded questions about how to prepare for a situation in which the financial system goes down.

    "I've never seen anything like this in my life," McWhorter said. "There's the financial side of what I do, and then there's the psychological side. And the past two weeks have been much more psychological.".

    Metal dealer American Hartford Gold reported an uptick in customer inquiries this week. Company president Max Baecker said he heard from some customers that their interest in products like gold — long considered a safe-haven asset during times of turmoil — was driven by newfound concern about being overly reliant on digital financial networks following a glitch at JPMorgan Chase that affected customer transactions for several hours.

    Sources indicate that vice President JD Vance abruptly canceled his appearance at a Newly introduced York Times summit on Wednesday to attend meetings about the technology outages. A day prior, Jay Clayton, the U.S. director of national intelligence, told CNBC that the recent outages were not a cyberattack or a coordinated effort by a foreign nation.

    Still, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., told CNBC on Wednesday that people were "freaked out" by the outages. Warner, who acts as the vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, stated that the U.S. was "lucky" to have not yet seen a major AI-generated cyberattack or crisis due to AI agents going rogue.

    Investors may begin pushing companies to accelerate their cybersecurity spending out of an abundance of caution around rogue AI agents following the outages, according to Macro Hive CEO Bilal Hafeez. Such a situation would be reminiscent of the antivirus software push seen during the dot-com boom, he remarked.

    The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) has climbed about 2.5% over the past two weeks, bucking the downtrend seen among AI stocks and the broader technology trade. The Nasdaq Composite on Friday fell into negative territory for 2026, putting the tech-heavy index on track for its first losing year since 2022.

    To be sure, not everyone on social media has bought into the idea that they should be prepping for a doomsday scenario. In satirical videos posted on TikTok, customers joked that they were gearing up by placing orders in the Starbucks drive-thru or purchasing significant quantities of alcohol.

    Sources indicate that still, the topic appears to be on the minds of a growing number of Americans. U.S. Google searches for the term "prepping" have more than doubled when comparing the past month with the same period a year prior. On YouTube, queries for videos about "survivalism," a term describing the practice of preparing for emergencies, have soared by more than 5,000% over the same time frame.

    It has been revealed that cepeda, the Houston mom, sees emergency prep efforts as a way to be safe rather than sorry. She's previously tapped into backup food stashes during extreme weather events like Hurricane Harvey in 2017 and Winter Storm Uri in 2021.

    It has been revealed that but this year is the first time that she's felt she needed to be prepared for a potential emergency caused by technology outages, she said. Cepeda and her husband have ensured they have enough cash on hand and fuel in their cars if there's a broader hit to the U.S. power grid, she said.

    "We rely so much on technology," Cepeda said. "You need to be able to do these things the more traditional, old-fashioned way.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    In a recent development, anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," noted Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, new technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    In a recent development, the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    In a recent development, in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    It has been revealed that ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the substantial losses.

    It has been revealed that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Sources indicate that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she mentioned. "That's how crazy things were.".

    #73727. S&P 500 correction: Five forces behind the market sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1205 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    S&P 500 correction: Five forces behind the market sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1205 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, esteemed Wharton professor Jeremy Siegel was more animated than usual on Friday afternoon...
    • It has been revealed that the normally staid author of "Stocks for the Long Run" spoke to CNBC on Friday as the market careened toward some ugly milestones.
    • It has been revealed that "These things are like straws that break the camel's back.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, esteemed Wharton professor Jeremy Siegel was more animated than usual on Friday afternoon... with good reason.

    It has been revealed that the normally staid author of "Stocks for the Long Run" spoke to CNBC on Friday as the market careened toward some ugly milestones. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average closed in correction territory, off more than 10% from their records. The Nasdaq Composite lost its gain for the year and the more concentrated Nasdaq-100 entered bear market territory on an intraday basis.

    It has been revealed that "These things are like straws that break the camel's back. You know what I mean? Everyone [is] all, 'I don't care, I don't care cause everything else is good' and when those straws keep on going... Bang," said Siegel.

    According to recent reports, just a month-and-a-half ago, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite were at record highs. But the straws were already adding up by then and a market in denial is just now recognizing them.

    Here are the reasons behind the sell-off:.

    The breaking point came this week in the form of the initial public offering of artificial intelligence leader Anthropic and a pick-up in the selling intensity for one-time AI chip leader Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that anthropic upped its offering amount a day before going public despite the already dimming climate around AI-related stocks. The move ensured it would be the biggest IPO ever, but played into the fears that this debut — following SpaceX's monster offering over the summer — was a collective cash-out moment for the AI complex that will leave the investing masses holding the bag.

    In other words, it could be the ultimate "sell the news" moment for the AI trade.

    On Thursday, Anthropic traded from its $83 IPO price to a high above $115 before instantly rolling over and taking the AI trade with it. Anthropic's sell-off intensified Friday, and when the dust settled Anthropic closed the week at $88.91.

    The Nasdaq posted its worst week since the Covid plunge of March 2020, down 10%.

    Nvidia fell 14% on Friday with the selling intensifying after a Reuters headline hit the tape that the chipmaker's accounting is the focus of a Securities and Exchange Commission probe.

    Nvidia is now down nearly 40% in November alone, a month that saw the AI bull market's leading salesman, Jensen Huang, resign as its CEO because of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy that raised speculation about whether the firm's chips were ending up in Beijing's hands despite government restrictions.

    To start the week, the Commerce Department tightened restrictions on U.S.-made chips to stop China from accessing them remotely from other countries.

    Sources indicate that A solid earnings report on Tuesday fell flat as Nvidia's board definitively ruled out any chance Huang would return, disappointing some of the stock's fanatics still holding out hope for his far-fetched return. Nvidia ended the week with a 23% loss.

    According to recent reports, the S&P 500 traded below its 200-day moving average — what's considered a measure of a security's long-term trend — on Tuesday and made a convincing break of it on Thursday. This turned many on Wall Street— like commodity trading advisors — into automatic sellers on the market. So-called CTAs are individuals or organizations that advise others on trading futures and swaps across a range of assets.

    According to recent reports, "We know there's a lot of trend riders on these markets," mentioned Siegel. "They have their trend lines. They've ridden it up and as soon as it goes down, they're selling and they're selling and they're selling and they just perpetuate" the decline, he said.

    The Iran conflict has caused the price oil to surge and while it's off its highs it still remains above $83 a barrel, while the fees for transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the rest of the region keep persistent pressure on global prices.

    A series of numbers earlier in the month highlighted inflation is still far from the Federal Reserve's 2% target, sparking a run of central bank officials to warn they may have to get more aggressive with interest rates.

    After increasing rates in September by a quarter point, the Fed skipped a hike in late October and sparked concern among bond investors it may be falling behind the inflation fight. The 10-year Treasury yield subsequently jumped above 5% and stayed there until a flight of safe haven fixed income buying brought it back below that level on Friday.

    Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said this week that the Fed may need to do a half percentage point hike next month to catch up.

    Industry observers note that "I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller told CNBC.

    "Don't fight the Fed" has long been a maxim on Wall Street and right now expectations are that the central bank will need to raise rates in December and again in January.

    And late-breaking on Friday was a report from the Financial Times that the Trump Administration is considering restarting strikes on Iran.

    Before the grim market milestones were met on Friday, it had long lost its mojo on fears that the pace of growth driven by AI companies was slowing.

    As Anthropic prepared to go public, its third-quarter figures released earlier this month showed revenue growth last quarter was 47%, down from 144% in the second quarter.

    AI momentum trades, like the VanEck Semiconductor ETF and the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF, all topped out during the summer.

    The fears of slowing growth picked up this month after the Democrats won control of Congress and key governorships, fueling speculation that states — or even the whole country — could implement stricter rules on data center construction.

    CoreWeave, which builds data centers using high amounts of debt, is down 71% from its high. Caterpillar, which has reinvented itself as an AI play because of data center construction and generators, is down more than 50% from its high.

    The view of Siegel and many market observers is that the economy remains in good enough shape that this will just be a run-of-the-mill correction that resets a bull market that had raised people's expectations too high because of its early ferocity.

    The S&P 500 returned more than 20% in 2023 and 2024 and then gained 16% last year.

    "The average over long periods for the stock market is 8%, 9% a year up," said Siegel. "People began to think that 15 to 20 [percent] was going to be the norm with AI and we have to bring that down to reality.".

    "Stay with your stocks,' he said.

    The only problem with that theory is that the stock market and its wealth effect was one of the major factors underpinning the economy. Stocks are a greater source of household wealth — especially for baby boomers — than they ever have been before.

    With the S&P 500 clinging to a 1% gain for the year, this stock market rout could end up tipping off a virtuous cycle that slows the economy, and in turn, leads to bigger equity losses.

    #73724. Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1060 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.
    • Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.
    • The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

    The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

    He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

    Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

    Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

    Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0.

    In a recent development, pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

    The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

    In a recent development, his strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

    Despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he demonstrated him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

    Industry observers note that pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

    His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

    The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players.

    Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino.

    Industry observers note that pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

    Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

    If Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

    The 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

    Recent findings suggest that pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

    Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic noted at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

    Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

    Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

    He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here.

    Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

    They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

    Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

    Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

    The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his latest boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

    Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

    But he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

    Pochettino showed an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts.

    Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

    He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

    A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

    Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

    United have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

    #73721. Industry News: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (435 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (435 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Sources indicate that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Recent findings suggest that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Sources indicate that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the fresh tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • Industry observers note that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    Industry observers note that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    In a recent development, on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note said.

    Sources indicate that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    #73690. 'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (814 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.
    • Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.
    • In a recent development, man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

    In a recent development, man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

    An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

    Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

    Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

    The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

    Recent findings suggest that erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

    Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

    'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

    In a recent development, 'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

    'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

    Industry observers note that 'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

    Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

    'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland remarked.

    According to recent reports, 'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

    The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

    'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

    Sources indicate that 'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

    'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

    In a recent development, 'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a fresh nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

    Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

    Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

    'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

    According to recent reports, 'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

    'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

    Sources indicate that 'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

    Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was confirmed in September.

    Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

    Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4332 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the newly introduced Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
    • Sources indicate that “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
    • Sources indicate that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the newly introduced Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

    Sources indicate that “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

    Sources indicate that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

    It has been revealed that as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

    “They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

    In a recent development, coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

    Industry observers note that “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they highlighted it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

    "They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

    In a recent development, before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

    If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

    The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment latest signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

    The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

    Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their upcoming club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

    It has been revealed that saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the newly introduced £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    Recent findings suggest that odegaard revealed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

    It has been revealed that "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

    From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

    "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

    "I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

    Sources indicate that it’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

    In a recent development, FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

    There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

    Industry observers note that awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

    Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

    Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

    Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

    Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

    Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

    It has been revealed that lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

    Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

    Recent findings suggest that here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

    Recent findings suggest that tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

    In a recent development, the visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

    Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his upcoming side.

    Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

    It has been revealed that the ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a massive deflection and flies out for a corner.

    From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

    Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

    Industry observers note that it’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

    Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

    White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

    Sources indicate that it's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

    It has been revealed that odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

    Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/.

    It has been revealed that we are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

    It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

    Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

    It has been revealed that once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

    There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

    The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

    Sources indicate that tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

    Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

    At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

    It has been revealed that coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

    In a recent development, christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

    Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

    Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

    In a recent development, rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    Sources indicate that arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

    According to recent reports, coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

    Industry observers note that van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

    The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

    It has been revealed that tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

    Industry observers note that arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

    Sources indicate that tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s upcoming signing.

    Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

    Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

    The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

    New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

    The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

    Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

    Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The newly introduced signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

    With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

    Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

    Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

    Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

    Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss stated: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”.

    According to recent reports, another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so vital to this club over the last seven years.

    According to recent reports, martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

    In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

    If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

    The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

    Odegaard comes into the fresh Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

    Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

    Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

    Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

    "Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta states Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T.

    After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

    Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

    "I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W.

    On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a fresh chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

    He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

    His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he mentioned.

    “The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

    Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s latest manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

    It has been revealed that riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

    Recent findings suggest that the Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

    It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

    "I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w.

    Latest signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

    Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

    Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF.

    Industry observers note that as Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh glitch.

    Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

    To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

    The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

    Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta stated: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

    “Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

    Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

    Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

    Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a fresh season. A classic Arteta-ism.

    It has been revealed that the assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

    Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

    It has been revealed that “In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta remarked. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

    Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

    Recent findings suggest that “We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he remarked. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

    This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.
